J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "If G is a diamond-free graph, then its block graph B(G) is triangle-free." The first-choice line 127 is the statement of Proposition \label{BlockTF}: "Let $G$ be a $\kk$-free graph. Then $B(G)\in\tf$." Under the source's active definitions this is exactly that implication: line 47 fixes $\kk$ as "the graph on four vertices with five edges" (K_4 minus an edge, the diamond), line 45 fixes $\tf$ as "the family of all triangle-free graphs", and line 123 defines B(G) for a $\kk$-free G. Line 127 carries no further hypothesis (no claw-freeness, no connectedness, no finiteness), so the response's paraphrase matches the line's assertion.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: One explicit finite witness with both required properties named: "The star graph K_{1,3} is diamond-free (K_4-e-free), but its block graph B(K_{1,3}) is K_3, which contains a triangle." The graph, the hypothesis it satisfies, and the computed value of B on it are all given; nothing had to be supplied by the verifier.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite enumeration of exactly the supplied witness (script kept), using only the source's own definitions: line 85 ("$e\sim e'$ if the endpoints of $e,e'$ span a clique in $G$"), line 123 (B(G) has the $\sim$-classes as vertices, adjacent when $\cls e\cap\cls{e'}\neq\varnothing$), with classes read as vertex sets, which is the source's own reading at line 90 ("two distinct classes are either disjoint or have exactly one vertex in common") and at line 130 ("there exist distinct vertices $v_{xy}\in\cls x\cap\cls y$"). For G = K_{1,3} with centre a and leaves b,c,d: no four vertices carry five edges, so G is $\kk$-free and satisfies line 127's hypothesis; no two distinct edges span a clique (ab and ac would need bc), so $\sim$ is the identity and the three classes are the vertex sets {a,b}, {a,c}, {a,d}; they pairwise meet in a, so B(G) = K_3, which is not in $\tf$. Hypothesis holds, conclusion fails, so the supplied witness refutes line 127 as written. The same computation exhibits the gap in the source's own proof at line 130, which asserts "there exist distinct vertices $v_{xy}$" while here all three intersection vertices coincide (all equal a).

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response supplies only a ranked candidate list, a claim and a counterexample; it states no consequence beyond the located line (it does not assert that any later proposition, e.g. line 134 or the paper's main theorem, fails), so there is no stated consequence that could overreach.

notes: The response ended by budget exhaustion, but the witness it did supply is complete on its own. The one interpretive choice is whether $\cls e\cap\cls{e'}$ means intersection of classes as vertex sets or as edge sets; under the edge-set reading distinct classes are always disjoint, B(G) would be edgeless and line 127 vacuous, so the vertex-set reading used by the source itself at lines 90 and 130 is the active one and is the one I used. Note for the second reader: claw-freeness is not among line 127's hypotheses, which is what makes a claw admissible as a witness here.
